text:
maya: FYI rolled anchor-shelf reserve from 8% -> 14% at 09:07 UTC as part of capacity tuning. Immediately saw tiny-gang pending spike and noisy preempts.

sam: which cluster/region?

maya: ap-southeast1, a few jobs bounced to us-west2. Warm pool resize also kicked (infra-bot) ~09:06.

noah: timeline sounds like a race. anchors reduced packing slack for tiny-gangs -> scheduler preempt cascade. Any taint churn?

maya: yes, several nodes got the new `reserved-anchor=true` taint applied, but some long-running GPU pods tolerate=false. Pods wouldn't co-locate.

jen: saw exploded eviction metrics on dashboards: gpu_evictions_per_min went from 0.5 -> 13 in 20m.

infra-bot: [autoscaler] warmpool resize +18 nodes requested in ap-southeast1 (req id: wp/2026-03-22/11).

sam: can you paste a pending pod event?

maya: here's a short excerpt from `kubectl describe pod ml-job-7`:
```
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m   default-scheduler  37/120 nodes are available: 34 Insufficient gpu, 3 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 28 node(s) had preemption risk.
  Normal   BackOff          30s  kubelet            Back-off pulling image
```

noah: ugh. two contributing issues: (1) anchor taints are effectively hard reservations that block gang co-location, (2) warmpool resize timing means new nodes weren't ready to receive pods, so scheduler overrelied on preempting.

olivia: mitigation suggestions?

sam: immediate: roll anchor reserve back to 8% (or make it soft) and pause warmpool scaling. Also throttle preemptor controller (reduce aggressive preempt loop).

noah: second-order: run a one-off compaction job to evict best-effort scatterers that hold GPU slots. Example: `kubectl delete -n infra pod -l workload=beam-worker --grace-period=0 --force --field-selector=status.phase=Running` — do 5-10 at a time.

maya: rolling back now. switching reserve to 8% (09:18 UTC).

jen: while rollback happens, can we snapshot `node.labels` + `node taints` and render a quick heatmap? I can run a script and paste a URL.

olivia: yep please do. add a new gauge: `gpu_fragmentation_ratio` = 1 - (max_packed_gangs / ideal_gangs) so flips can be blocked.

infra-bot: [config] anchor-shelf-reserve changed to 8% by maya (change id: deploy/2026-03-22/843).

sam: policy idea: scheduler could temporarily ignore anchor taints for pods with `scheduling.k8s.redwood/preempt-level=high` and `spec.podTopologySpread`=gang. Or introduce `preferGangCoLocation` boolean.

noah: tradeoffs: ignoring anchors harms reserved workloads; we need a fallthrough rule that only allows this when pending gangs > X and fragmentation ratio > Y.

jen: postmortem checklist item: 1) add canary ramp for reserve flips (5m) 2) guard metric gpu_fragmentation_ratio 3) coordinate warmpool operations in same change window.

maya: observed after rollback: evictions tapering, pending gangs back to ~1.2x baseline in 12m. Marking as mitigated but opening follow-ups.

olivia: I'll create a short runbook section "reserve flips" with `kubectl` queries and the heatmap link. Also add a small script to query `kubectl get pods -A -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}:{.spec.affinity}{"\n"}{end}'` for quick affinity scans.

sam: add this to CI for the reserve flag: a dry-run that simulates packing with current cluster snapshot and fails if fragmentation delta > 10%.

noah: action items assigned: olivia -> runbook + canary gating, sam -> reserve flip dry-run, jen -> telemetry gauge, maya -> post-change rollback safety net.

maya: thanks all. keep an eye on ap-southeast1 for the next hour. :thumbsup:
